chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Yaqub ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mu'tab ibn al-Mubarak, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a Thursday while he was undergoing phlebotomy (hijama). I asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of God, do you undergo phlebotomy on a Thursday?' He said, 'Yes. Whoever among you undergoes phlebotomy, let him do so on a Thursday, for on the evening of every Friday, the blood moves in scattered portions due to the Resurrection, and it does not return to its nest until the morning of Thursday.' Then he turned to his servant Rabih and said, 'O Rabih, hold the cup firmly, make the cupping glass soft, and make the incision a creeping one.' And Abu Abdillah said, 'Whoever undergoes phlebotomy on the last Thursday of the month in the early part of the day, the disease will leave him completely.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of undergoing phlebotomy on Thursdays in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the physical act of hijama to eschatological events, specifically the gathering of souls and blood on the Day of Resurrection. The detailed instructions on cupping technique reflect the Shia emphasis on combining spiritual merit with precise medical practice, while the specific benefit for the last Thursday of the month highlights the cyclical nature of purification in the lunar calendar.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-80 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Marvan ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Ma’tab ibn al-Mubarak, “

Once I went to see Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) on a Thursday. He was having phlebotomy performed. I asked him, ‘O (grand)son of the Prophet! Are you having phlebotomy done on a Thursday?’ He (MGB) replied, ‘Yes, It is fine for anyone to have phlebotomy done on a Thursday since there is some movement of blood on Friday nights due to the fear of the Resurrection which doesn’t return to its original place until Thursday morning.’ He (MGB) then faced his servant Rabih (who was performing the phlebotomy) and told him, ‘O Rabih! Stick in the phlebotomy tool firmly, cup slowly and cut lightly.’ Then he (MGB) said, ‘Pain would totally leave the body of whoever has phlebotomy done early in the morning on the last Thursday of the month.’”
